package_info.why_malicious: The package was deliberately created to impersonate the legitimate 'localforage-memoryStorageDriver' package by using an all-lowercase name, exploiting NPM's case sensitivity. This is a typosquatting attack intended to deceive users into installing a malicious or placeholder package instead of the authentic one, potentially leading to supply chain compromise or disruption.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: N/A (malicious behavior is in the package naming and impersonation, not in code content)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At install-time, the package name is crafted to closely mimic a legitimate package by using all lowercase letters, exploiting case sensitivity to deceive users and automated systems into installing the wrong package, resulting in potential supply chain compromise or disruption.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The package name is intentionally designed to be visually indistinguishable from a widely used legitimate package, differing only in capitalization. This is a textbook typosquatting/impersonation tactic that targets users who may not notice the case difference.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages are expected to have unique, non-confusing names that do not exploit case sensitivity to impersonate other packages. This package violates those expectations by deliberately mimicking another package's name except for letter case.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate forks or variants may use similar names, but do not intentionally exploit case sensitivity to deceive users or impersonate another package.
key_indicators: Package name differs from a popular package only by capitalization (e.g., 'localforage-memorystoragedriver' vs 'localforage-memoryStorageDriver')
No legitimate codebase or project associated with the package
Package is published as a 'security holding' or placeholder after removal
Publication date is after the legitimate package, indicating opportunistic impersonation

attack_chain.action: Attacker publishes a package with a name that is visually identical to a legitimate package except for capitalization (e.g., 'localforage-memorystoragedriver' vs 'localforage-memoryStorageDriver'), exploiting NPM's case sensitivity.
attack_chain.leads_to: Users or automated systems are deceived into installing the malicious or placeholder package instead of the legitimate one.

attack_chain.action: User or automated system installs the maliciously named package, believing it to be the legitimate one due to the near-identical name.
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential execution of malicious code, supply chain disruption, or installation of a non-functional placeholder, depending on the attacker's intent.

behavioral_signatures: Package names that differ from popular packages only by capitalization (case-only typosquatting)
Recently published packages with names matching existing mixed-case packages in all lowercase
Packages with no legitimate code or with 'security holding' placeholders after removal
Packages published shortly after a legitimate package gains popularity
file_indicators: package.json with a name field matching a popular package except for case
Absence of meaningful code or presence of placeholder content in index.js or main entry file
No associated repository or project homepage
network_indicators: N/A (attack is based on package naming, not network behavior)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Continuously monitor new package publications for names that match existing packages except for capitalization. Use automated tools to compare new package names against a list of existing packages with mixed-case names and flag potential impersonation attempts. Alert on packages with no meaningful code or those published as 'security holding' placeholders, especially if their names closely resemble popular packages. Cross-reference publication dates to identify opportunistic impersonation following legitimate package updates.
